title: Over-Generalized Interface Hiding Fault Semantics (Exception Masking)
pattern: Swallowing fine-grained boundary errors (network failures, DB lock timeouts) to expose a generic, error-free API representation.
why_bad: Callers cannot build robust retry mechanisms, fallbacks, or security logging because vital structural failure details are discarded.
detection: Match block matchers or `Result` helpers (`map_err`, `and_then`) that map complex error structs into simple `None` or generic `Err("Error")` at boundaries.
counterexample: Security gates intentionally sanitizing diagnostic errors to prevent exposing internal details to public users.
fix:
Define rich, context-specific error types at layer boundaries.
```rust
enum BoundaryError {
    Timeout,
    Unauthenticated,
    FormatCorrupted(String),
}
```
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design* by John K. Ousterhout (Chapter 6, "Masking Exceptions", p. 119).
